newsitem.title: JORDAN: U.S. military commander meets Jordan's king.
newsitem.headline: U.S. military commander meets Jordan's king.

text.p: The commander of U.S. forces in the Middle East General Binford Peay met Jordan's King Hussein and senior military officials on Monday on the final leg of a tour of regional allies, the U.S. embassy in Amman said.
An embassy official declined to give details of Peay's talks, but said he met Field Marshall Abdul-Hafez Kaabneh before joining the monarch for lunch.
Peay, Commander-in-Chief of the U.S. Central Command, visited Gulf Arab allies Saudi Arabia, Kuwait and Bahrain before flying to Jordan, which also has close military ties with Washington.

Jordan took delivery of $100 million worth of U.S. military equipment last December and is due to receive the first batch of a squadron of F-16 fighter-bombers worth $200 million by the end of the year.

The United States launched a revamp of Jordan's armed forces in recognition of its new role in the Middle East after King Hussein signed a 1994 peace treaty with Israel and turned against his former ally President Saddam Hussein of Iraq.
